rv.q: “Little Women: The Musical,” a pleasant but staid revisitation that’s too leisurely in locating the heart of the material.

Though Ms. Foster shows winning flashes of a previously undetected gift for fresh comic line readings, theatergoers not enamored of unstinting eagerness may find her energy less infectious than exhausting.
Despite its flaws, Little Women moved and entertained us.

cn.t: Sutton Foster dazzles as Jo March in this old-fashioned adaptation, but critics find the musical itself pleasant yet uninspired—a star vehicle that doesn't quite match its leading lady's golden-age Broadway chops.

vs.sum: The August Wilson Theatre offers good sightlines from most seats, although the rake isn't steep, which can cause issues if seated behind taller patrons. The theater has average comfort with decent legroom but tight seats. Its Italian-inspired design and cozy feel enhance the ambiance, making it a pleasant venue overall. Facilities are adequate, with standard amenities and helpful staff.

acc.note: Stair lift to orchestra; elevator between orchestra and mezzanine. Infrared headsets available.
